title: Pahlavi Texts, Part IV: Contents of the Nasks
attributionNote: The Denkard is an anonymous ninth-century Pahlavi encyclopaedia of Zoroastrian learning, compiled by several hands. Book VIII summarises the lost Nasks, the twenty-one books of the Avesta.
description: Book VIII of the Denkard is the ancient world's most detailed catalogue of a scripture: it summarises, book by book, the contents of the twenty-one Nasks of the Avesta, most of which are lost. The volume adds selections from the Denkard and Zad-sparam on the same Nasks, including the Vistasp Nask, the Vendidad Nask and the Hadokht Nask, and the Rivayat excerpts that preserve their memory.
historicalContext: The Denkard was compiled in the ninth century to preserve Zoroastrian learning under Islamic rule. Because the Nasks themselves survive only in fragments, West's translation (Sacred Books of the East, volume 37, 1892) remains a primary source for the lost Avesta.
availabilityNote: Complete for this volume. Book VIII of the Denkard (46 chapters) and Book IX (69 chapters), with the accompanying selections from Zad-sparam and the Rivayats, are streamed from the Internet Sacred Text Archive at read time, one chapter per page. The volume's introduction and editorial observations are not part of the work.
